Saladin, however, sent to Alexandria
and also brought for himself large ships,
and stationed them opposite the harbor (harbors) of Tyre.
Then, on one of the nights, the seafarers came out in swift small boats,
and they shattered many of the large ships of the Arabs (Muslims).
And they captured two of their famous western ship-captains,
while the rest threw themselves into the sea and drowned;
and others began to flee in their ships towards Beirut.
And the Franks overtook them also,
and captured most of them,
while others were cast into the sea.
And when Saladin saw this disaster, and the vigor of those who came out also on dry land to fight,
it became wearisome to him and to those who were with him;
and they burned the siege towers (wooden towers) that they had built, and the mangonels, and some of the ships that were left behind,
and he departed from Tyre and went to Acre.
And he gave an order to his armies
that every man should go to his region,
and rest (as it were, to rest) in his house.
At that time there arose a quarrel between the Caliph al-Nasir and Saladin,
on the grounds that Saladin had cut off the tribute that was due to the Caliph upon Syria,
and even from Egypt, when he took it, he sent nothing.
And also on the grounds that when Saladin was drunk, he used to say:
"I am prepared to abolish the proclamation of that one in Baghdad,
and restore the proclamation of the Fatimids who formerly were in Egypt."
The Caliph al-Nasir was further grieved
in that a certain man of low birth from among the Baghdadites,
who was in the service of Saladin,
Saladin sent as an envoy bearing the good news of the capture of Jerusalem to him.
And in that same year, a certain Turkmen man from among the nomads (shepherds), whose name was Rustam,
assembled for himself five thousand Turkmen horsemen,
and also many foot soldiers,
and entered Cilicia to take spoil and to plunder.
Then Leo (Levon), the ruler of Cilicia, when he perceived them,
seized against them the mountain passes (kleisourai) in the region of Marash,
and destroyed them all with the edge of the sword.
